finding: A prior integration attempted to import assert_submittable from validate.py before that shared API existed, so tests could not import the submission writer.
action: The shared validator/writer API is present in the current checkout. At the final merge review, the full pytest suite passed 70/70 tests with no warnings reported.

finding: Older tests used the sibling gems57 package name and an earlier uniqueness API; earlier uniqueness reporting also treated Jaccard as a clearance threshold.
action: The current gate uses signed full-footprint Spearman >0.90 OR one-sided positive support >70% within 3 pixels. Jaccard is diagnostic only. Regression tests cover the public wrapper's expected-grid/progress-log path and fail-closed incomplete inventory, missing SHA-256 pins, and malformed rows; all 70 current tests pass, including empty-prior edge handling, local-link validation, and fail-closed status-page regression tests.

finding: Three data layouts (data/official, data/bridge, data/raw) were expected by different code generations, while the link directories are git-ignored, so a fresh clone could fail.
action: prepare_data.py creates data/bridge and data/raw links from the prepared source tree; the recorded data-preparation evidence documents the layout.

finding: Earlier reports treated the catalogue-frame holdout/live-score anti-correlation as an inverted instrument. Catalogue-pruned leaderboard artifacts can be rewarded by a catalogue holdout for construction reasons, so the relationship does not validate hidden-truth recovery.
action: The proxy protocol withholds whole mapped segments, derives features only from the visible catalogue, applies pixel-exact masks, and compares against unpruned registry rasters and matched random lines. Report all values as HOLDOUT-DTI, never organizer scores.

finding: A 311,617-pixel prior raster puts 95.8182% of the footprint within 3 pixels. H61-G final dots have 98.5925% one-sided overlap; H61-L pre-placement scarp-ribbon support has 94.6692%. Both exceed the explicit 70% stop threshold although their Jaccard values are small. No saved pre-placement uniqueness receipt was found for the archived H61-G output; its final-dot failure independently blocks submission.
action: Removed the unauthorized dense-reference/Jaccard exception. The shared fail-closed gate counts every strictly positive candidate cell, checks both pre-placement surface and final raster against every raster in the declared inventory, and stops for signed Spearman >0.90 OR one-sided 3-pixel overlap >0.70. Missing inventory paths, hashes, or grid matches cannot clear a candidate. Do not infer an H61-G pre-placement pass: its archival receipt is absent, and its measured final-dot failure is sufficient to stop.

finding: Older root and site pages advertised conflicting primary downloads and status; one historic page called H61-G ready despite the strict uniqueness failure, and main carried a file under docs/submissions/.
action: The current README, root redirect, and evidence-driven docs builder say no TIFF is cleared. The linked H61-G GeoTIFF is diagnostic-only. The current H61-L screen stopped pre-placement; separate archived H61-L/H61-M/H61-X and docs/submissions TIFFs fail the literal final-dot gate and are marked historical/not approved. Every non-current HTML page is visibly marked HISTORICAL PAGE — SUPERSEDED, states that legacy READY/UNIQUE labels are not clearance, and links to the current status and strict artifact audit.

finding: Earlier wording described the production inversion as damped/converged, and described the recorded six-step experiment as divergent. Neither claim is supported by the artifacts.
action: Production is documented as the first low-passed Bouguer-slab iterate. The six-step trace's residual decreases, but the final maximum change remains about 130.5 m against a 1 m tolerance; nonlinear convergence is unverified, not proven impossible.

finding: The historical H61-G candidate is a point/dot artifact, not a 3×3 multi-line ribbon submission. The current H61-L scarp-ribbon surface failed pre-placement, so that run produced no holdout or TIFF. Main also contains a separate archived H61-L ribbon/dot TIFF and HOLDOUT-DTI receipt from work performed under the older gate.
action: Keep the current-run stop distinct from the archived result. The archived H61-L score remains HOLDOUT-DTI proxy evidence (0.044330; CI 0.041405–0.047832; 22,641 positives; gems61.holdout_segmented v2) but its final TIFF fails strict one-sided overlap at 98.6375%, so it is not eligible or cleared. No current output is represented as a cleared ribbon artifact.

finding: Earlier parallel work left duplicate uniqueness helper definitions and multiple pages claiming a primary candidate.
action: The current status renderer derives one submission verdict from evidence and marks older generated pages HISTORICAL PAGE — SUPERSEDED and links them to current status plus the strict audit. After adding fail-closed SHA-256 validation and malformed-row handling, all 70 tests pass; generated current pages are rebuilt from the corrected irregularities record.

finding: The sandbox allow-list prevents some direct organizer/raw-host downloads; public mirror data are not equivalent to an organizer receipt.
action: Input provenance classes and hashes are recorded in data-preparation and lidar-source evidence. No data fetch or owner report is presented as an organizer-confirmed score.

finding: The group/owner-reported H33-2-b2 score 0.2778 is not bound to exact artifact bytes by a located organizer receipt.
action: Keep 0.2778 labeled group/owner-reported and unverified. The public leaderboard is stated separately, with the 2026-10-11 fetch showing #1 = 0.4133 and #8 = 0.3195.

finding: An earlier registry fetch list used a wrong suffix for one GEMSDOE57 raster and left a declared public comparison path unavailable. The original H61-G/H61-L run-time inventory also predated the later main-branch TIFFs.
action: Centralized 21 public paths in scripts/registry_sources.tsv and added hash/grid-checked indexing over docs/downloads, docs/submissions, and out. The current inventory contains 21 declared public paths plus 11 local TIFFs (32 records), not the organizer's complete registry. The original 28-record H61-G/H61-L run-time manifest is preserved separately; any inventory error must fail closed.

finding: The current H61-L attempt used a public 12-band terrain-descriptor derivative based on USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM work, not raw lidar and not a fault prediction. Its 614,556-pixel scarp-ribbon surface has 94.6692% one-sided 3-pixel overlap with the dense prior.
action: Source URL, upstream commit/blob, metadata, and local SHA-256 are recorded. This current-run candidate stopped before holdout, placement, or TIFF writing; no current-run H61-L HOLDOUT-DTI is claimed. A separate main-branch H61-L variant has a historical holdout result but fails the strict final-dot gate; see IR-61-RIBBON-01 and evidence/local_artifact_strict_dot_audit.json.

finding: The historical H61-G run card records 3 candidate/budget experiments; the H61-L pre-placement surface screen adds 1 if the cap is counted across the entire workflow. A strict aggregate count is therefore 4, beyond a 3-experiment ceiling.
action: Flag the aggregate count explicitly. No additional model or holdout experiment was run during this review; stop further candidate experiments and do not spend a weekly slot. The elapsed-time cap was not independently measured. Legacy model/holdout CLI entrypoints without the current pre-placement check are retired; the H61-G direct holdout stage now applies the shared strict surface gate to every arm first. No new model or holdout result was run to make this safeguard.

finding: After merging main, four archived TIFFs had status/evidence produced under an alternative dense-reference/Jaccard or legacy overlap policy. A strict literal final-dot audit measured H61-L 98.6375%, H61-M 94.6836%, H61-X 98.7658%, and docs/submissions/61gemsdoe-basement-step-ribbon-20261011T054408Z.tif 99.1475% within 3 px of the prior basement-HGM raster. The same comparator stops all 10 local candidate TIFFs in downloads/submissions.
action: Retire the old UNIQUE labels for submission decisions. Keep all artifacts as historical/unapproved, retain the exact TIFFs for provenance, make no upload link appear as cleared, and use evidence/local_artifact_strict_dot_audit.json as the reproducible short-circuit dot-gate receipt. No rank test or new holdout was run after the measured strict overlap stop; no organizer registry completeness is claimed.
